question: If the line \(L\) in the \(xy\)-plane has half the slope and twice the \(y\)-intercept of the line \(y=\frac23x+4,\) then an equation for \(L\) is
solution:
In the form \(y=mx+b\), \(m\) is the slope and \(b\) is the \(y\)-intercept. Thus the given line has slope \(\frac23\) and \(y\)-intercept \(4\).

For line \(L\), the slope and intercept must be
\[
m=\frac12\cdot\frac23=\frac13,
\qquad b=2\cdot4=8.
\]
Putting these into \(y=mx+b\) gives
\[
\boxed{y=\frac13x+8},
\]
which is choice \(\boxed{\text{A}}\).

edges.reason: The description identifies b=0 as a proportional-function special case, but the tested linear-form and parameter criteria can be met from y=kx+b with k nonzero directly. Gemini promotes that contextual comparison into an extra required criterion; retain the useful special-case preparation.

The integer-multiplier case supplies a useful stepping stone and repeated-addition interpretation. The product-of-numerators/product-of-denominators rule follows directly from a part-of-a-part area model without executing the earlier decimal-free integer-multiplier procedure; Gemini confuses this customary progression with necessity.
